Luxury.manifesto: Most game studios race the calendar. We started The Holloway Studios in 2003 with a different premise: one game every five to seven years, designed by the founder, scored by the studio's resident composer, played by people who will wait. Two games shipped so far. The third is in year four.
Luxury.industrySummary: Premium long-arc game development has been claimed by AAA studios with seven-year cycles but rarely by small studios. There is a quieter market for the small heritage studio with multi-year cycles and a long-arc audience.

Corporate.mission: Independent studios need scale partners. Investors need a disciplined operator. We sit in the middle, professionalizing what was previously fragmented across many smaller players.
Corporate.vision: The opening is a structured, mid-size group with real operating discipline.
coreValues: Trustworthy — a core principle the brand operates by.

Strategic — a core principle the brand operates by.

Corporate.brandDescription: Highridge Gaming Group operates a portfolio of game studio brands with shared publishing, distribution, and back-office infrastructure.
Corporate.scope:
Highridge Gaming Group works across:
• Studio acquisition and partnership
• Multi-platform game publishing
• Shared marketing, distribution, and player support
• Live-services infrastructure across the portfolio
• Annual investor and operator reporting
Corporate.mission: To provide a serious operating platform for mid-tier studios that want to keep their identity and outsource the operations.
Corporate.vision: A multi-brand gaming operator where every studio's third game ships better than its first because the operations are shared.
coreValues: Senior — partners deal with partners.
Operational — the publishing stack runs around the clock.
Reliable — predictable terms, year over year.
Discreet — studio relationships stay between us and the studio.
Corporate.brandNameRationale: Highridge is a real American place-name with a holding-company register, paired with Gaming + Group following the multi-brand operator naming convention (Activision Blizzard, EA, Take-Two Interactive's structure). The pair reads as an institutional operator with regional roots and multi-brand portfolio.
Corporate.manifesto: Highridge Gaming Group owns and operates a portfolio of game studio brands. Each studio retains its identity, leadership, and creative direction; we operate the shared publishing infrastructure, distribution relationships, and back office. The buyer is a studio founder considering sale, a platform partner seeking single-vendor publishing relationships, or an institutional investor holding gaming assets.
Corporate.industrySummary: Game publishing has consolidated under a small number of large operators (EA, Activision Blizzard now within Microsoft, Take-Two, Embracer). The opening is for a regional mid-tier multi-brand gaming operator with strong studio relationships, modern publishing infrastructure, and the procurement-grade reliability platform partners and institutional investors require.
Corporate.competitorLandscape: Embracer Group (embracer.com) is the multi-brand reference at scale. Devolver Digital (devolverdigital.com) holds the indie publisher peer slot. Annapurna Interactive (annapurnainteractive.com) sits in the considered-indie publisher middle. tinyBuild (tinybuild.com) plays in the multi-brand mid-market position. We belong in the regional mid-tier multi-studio operator category.
Corporate.positioningStatement: Highridge Gaming Group is a regional multi-brand gaming operator running publishing, distribution, and shared operations across a portfolio of independent studios.
Corporate.positioningRationale: We compete on shared publishing infrastructure, platform relationships, and the operational reliability studio founders need without giving up creative direction.

Creative.tagline: A game studio built around the impossible time.
Creative.brandNameRationale: Speedrun is the real gaming community practice of completing a game as fast as possible. The definite article + Co suffix follows the considered-creative trade-name school.
Creative.manifesto: Most studios make games for the widest audience and round off the edges. Hard Mode makes games for the players who want the version with the edges intact. We design for the committed and assume the rest will find their way in.
Creative.industrySummary: Indie and mid-size game studios have been chasing accessibility. The opening at the other end is studios that lean into difficulty, depth, and demanding design. Players will buy them. They are already buying them.
Creative.competitorLandscape: FromSoftware (fromsoftware.jp) holds the cultural peak of difficulty-as-brand. ZA/UM (zaumstudio.com) before its troubles, did the literary difficult game. Cardboard Computer (cardboardcomputer.com) does the slow demanding side. We sit in their company, with a sharper visual brand.
Creative.positioningStatement: A studio that makes games for players who like the harder option.

targetAudience.primary: Players in their 20s and 30s who have completed at least one FromSoftware game. They wear the merch. They quote the boss fights. They tell other players they should try it.

dos: Be honest about how hard the game is
Quote real player frustrations in marketing
Make the merch feel earned
donts: Lower the floor of the experience

Creative.tagline: A game studio for the characters nobody plays.
Creative.brandDescription: The NPC Studio is a creative-led game studio building games entirely around the non-player characters — the shopkeepers, the side-quest givers, the people who watch the player walk past.
Creative.scope:
The NPC Studio works across:
• Single-game projects centred on non-player characters
• Procedurally-authored NPC dialog and behaviour systems
• Companion books published with each release
• Public devlogs documenting the design philosophy
• A weekly newsletter on game-narrative craft
Creative.mission: To make games whose most interesting characters are the ones the player never controls.
Creative.vision: A studio whose third game is taught in narrative-design classes for what it does with characters who never get a line.
coreValues: Literary — the writing is the work.
Specific — every NPC has a full interior life.
Warm — we treat the side cast with the dignity the player character usually gets.
Considered — we ship when the dialog is ready.
Creative.brandNameRationale: NPC is the universally-understood game acronym for Non-Player Character. Naming the studio after the secondary cast — the characters games usually deprioritize — stakes a clear creative position. The definite article + acronym + Studio format reads as a small declarative outfit (The Chinese Room spirit, Failbetter Games tone).
Creative.manifesto: Every game centres the player character. The merchant, the guard, the bartender, the farmer — the people the player walks past — are usually decoration. We started The NPC Studio because the more interesting question is what those characters do when the player isn't looking. The studio makes games where the side cast is the main story.
Creative.industrySummary: Narrative-led indie games have a recognized audience but most centre the player character. There is real space for a creative-led studio that explicitly inverts the focus — games structured around NPC interiority, with the player as the witness rather than the protagonist.
Creative.competitorLandscape: The Chinese Room (thechineseroom.co.uk) is the closest peer in narrative-led indie work. Failbetter Games (failbettergames.com) holds the dense-text peer slot. Inkle Studios (inklestudios.com) plays in the choice-based narrative middle. Telltale Games (telltale.com) is the legacy narrative-game reference. We sit alongside Inkle and Failbetter with a sharper NPC-focused premise.
Creative.positioningStatement: The NPC Studio is an indie game studio whose games centre the non-player characters and treat the player as a witness.
Creative.positioningRationale: The brand competes on the inversion. Every game we ship has a player character who is mostly an observer; the merchants, guards, and side-quest givers have full interior lives. The premise is the marketing.

motivations: Want games that take the secondary cast seriously.
Want a studio with a clear narrative philosophy.
Want to read after they finish playing.

dos: Write devlogs in the lead writer's voice.

Send a weekly newsletter on narrative-design craft.

Creative.tagline: A game studio for the moment you save.
Creative.brandDescription: Save Point Studios is a creative-led game studio building games centred entirely around the save mechanic — the moment a player decides what to preserve and what to lose.
Creative.scope:
Save Point Studios works across:
• Single-game projects centred on the save mechanic
• Save-system design as the primary creative work
• Published essays on save-state design philosophy
• Customer save-state archives across years
• Direct-to-player sales
Creative.mission: To treat the save point as a primary creative design object.
Creative.vision: A studio whose save-mechanic designs become standard references in game-design education.
coreValues: Literary — the writing about save-state design is part of the work.
Specific — every save mechanic is intentional.
Warm — the player's choice is honoured.
Considered — save states are preserved.
Creative.brandNameRationale: Save Point is the universal gaming-trade phrase for the point in a game where progress is preserved — naming the studio after the player's decisive moment. Studios is the plain category suffix. No 'The' prefix.
Creative.manifesto: Most games treat saving as a feature. We started Save Point Studios because the actual most decisive moment in any game is when the player decides what to save and what to risk.
Creative.industrySummary: Save-mechanic design is rarely treated as a primary creative work. There is real space for a creative-led studio that positions on save-state design.
Creative.competitorLandscape: The Chinese Room (thechineseroom.co.uk) plays the closest narrative peer. Failbetter Games (failbettergames.com) holds the dense-text peer slot. Inkle Studios (inklestudios.com) sits in the choice-based peer position. We sit alongside Inkle with sharper save-mechanic focus.
Creative.positioningStatement: Save Point Studios is an indie game studio building games centred on the save mechanic as the primary design decision.
Creative.positioningRationale: The brand competes on the save-state premise.
